geometry.note: detector is a coarser stand-in for the real one, same field of view
geometry.cor_definition: rotation axis projects at column (nu-1)/2 + cor_px (same as ct_recon's cor_px)

quartz.source: polychromatic: mu(E) from formula + density + NIST

hematite.source: polychromatic: mu(E) from formula + density + NIST

caveats: single effective energy, no beam hardening, scatter or spectrum
values tied to the listed densities
paper Table 2 values are calculated, not measured

spectrum.model: spectrum.py: Kramers continuum + tungsten K lines, Al/Cu filtration; calibrated to the paper's voltage-to-effective-energy table (fitted, not measured)
spectrum.detector: energy-integrating, weights ~ photon number x energy, no scintillator response

expected_in_reconstruction.note: POLYCHROMATIC: mu values are the apparent mu of a very thin sample (an upper bound) - beam hardening makes the reconstructed values LOWER, with cupping in the host (centre darker than the rim) and larger drops for thick or dense material. for ct_recon.py run with --bin 1 --step 1 and no --z. Indices are 0-based [z_slice, row, col]; Fiji shows slices 1-based. With --bin b divide positions by b. Values are mu in 1/mm (before the grey-range mapping).
